title: Canonical comparisons for successive open restriction of module sheaves and derived objects
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $T\subset V\subset U$ be open subsets, with inclusions $i:T\to V$ and $j:V\to U$. Write $R=\mathcal O_X$ and $\operatorname{Res}_i=\operatorname{SheafOfModules.overMap}(R,i)$ for restriction on the localized open sites. Define the canonical natural isomorphism $c_{i,j}:\operatorname{Res}_i\circ\operatorname{Res}_j\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}_{i\,;\,j}$, where the displayed composition applies restriction along $j$ first and then along $i$, by the identity on sections of every module sheaf. In the derived categories [def-pc-derived-category], define $c^D_{i,j}:D(\operatorname{Res}_i)\circ D(\operatorname{Res}_j)\xrightarrow{\sim}D(\operatorname{Res}_{i\,;\,j})$ by the inverse canonical comparison from deriving a composite, followed by the derived natural isomorphism induced by $c_{i,j}$. Thus both comparisons use the canonical sectionwise identity, with no additional choice of comparison maps.

def derivedModuleOpenMapCompIso (X : Scheme.{u}) {T V U : X.Opens}
    (i : T ⟶ V) (j : V ⟶ U)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over V))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over T))] :
    (SheafOfModules.overMap.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) j).mapDerivedCategory ⋙
      (SheafOfModules.overMap.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) i).mapDerivedCategory ≅
    (SheafOfModules.overMap.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) (i ≫ j)).mapDerivedCategory
